question: V versus V' class-membership in the IO reduced gauge sector

local_stack_findings.paper17: K_hat_g = K_gauge I is the generator of the coupled modular flow on the reduced thermal-gauge sector.
local_stack_findings.paper18_V: V(alpha) = -2 ln(cos alpha) is the unique smooth real logarithmic generator of the reduced gauge center.
local_stack_findings.paper18_B: First variation of open covariant transport reads dV and hence V'(alpha) = 2 gamma.
local_stack_findings.paper22_boundary: Scalarity alone does not force K_gauge; the missing step is observable class-membership into the GTTP-type one-slot positive transfer class.
local_stack_findings.paper23_boundary: Lemma 23.B preserves alpha = 1 for a zero-order bridge but does not by itself upgrade dV grammar to V grammar.

literature_findings.statement: A fixed faithful normal KMS state comes with a specific modular automorphism group. Replacing its generator by a different function generally changes the dynamics and, in equilibrium, the associated KMS state.

Relative or perturbed modular data are pair-of-state or perturbed-dynamics objects. The natural operator there is a relative Hamiltonian / cocycle, not a replacement modular generator for the original state.
The slogan 'infinitesimal means derivative of the modular generator' is too coarse. First-order variation of states can still read the fixed modular Hamiltonian itself.

synthesis.where_the_split_lives: The primary split is between fixed-state modular readout on the reduced gauge center and variational/relative-modular response on the tangent or cocycle side. Paper 16 degree counting is necessary but not sufficient, because both V and V' are compatible with degree-1 one-slot grammar. The bridge algebra and scalarization map decide which side the physical observable belongs to.
synthesis.challenge_to_current_heuristic: The right distinction is not finite versus infinitesimal in general. It is fixed modular flow versus variation of the generator/state family. BDP reads V' because it is explicitly a first variation of transport. GTTP reads V because it is a direct finite modular-flow readout of the chosen KMS state.

candidate_theorem.label: Conditional modular-versus-variational class-membership theorem
premises: The reduced thermal-gauge algebra is M_red = M_th tensor Z_g with Z_g = W*(K_hat_g).
The faithful normal reduced state omega_red has modular flow sigma_t with K_hat_g = V(alpha) I on the active gauge eigensector.
The observable family O is certified into one of two typed classes: modular-readout class or variational/relative class.
Scalarization preserves observable type whenever a scalar coefficient is extracted from O.
candidate_theorem.conclusion_modular_readout: If O is a positive one-slot transfer observable acted on by the fixed modular flow of omega_red, then its logarithmic coefficient is V(alpha), not V'(alpha).
candidate_theorem.conclusion_variational: If the physical observable is the first variation of a transport family or a relative-state intertwiner, then the linear coefficient is the tangent of the central character, dK_hat_g/dalpha = V'(alpha) I.
candidate_theorem.application: WMR closes if the weak-rate observable is proved to lie in the modular-readout class. The PSRP numerator closes if the seed covariance is proved to be a center-generated modular readout rather than a first-variation transport response or same-fiber self-intensity.

honest_boundaries: This memo gives a sharper theorem schema for the numerator split V versus V'.
It does not by itself derive the Paper 23 denominator 1/x for the primordial seed.

So a pure V-versus-V' theorem is enough to upgrade WMR, but it is not obviously enough to upgrade the full n_s claim unless the theorem is strengthened to include the 1-form transfer projection as well.
No existing theorem in the present stack yet proves that the weak-rate observable or the primordial seed covariance belongs to the fixed modular-readout class.

sources.label: Herman-Takesaki 1970
sources.role: For a faithful normal state, automorphisms commuting with the modular/KMS group leave the state invariant; the paper also treats KMS structure for quasi-free automorphisms of the CAR algebra.

sources.label: Araki 1971
sources.role: Quasifree states are characterized as the unique KMS state of a Bogoliubov automorphism of CAR.

sources.label: Bisognano-Wichmann 1976
sources.role: Canonical AQFT source for the statement that a specific modular automorphism group is tied to a specific geometric one-parameter flow for wedge algebras.

sources.label: Araki 1973
sources.role: Relative Hamiltonian / intertwiner formalism: when one compares two faithful normal states, the natural object is a relative modular cocycle between their modular groups.

sources.label: Derezinski-Jaksic-Pillet 2001
sources.role: Perturbing the dynamics by Q produces a perturbed dynamics and a new perturbed KMS state; changing the generator changes the equilibrium state.

sources.label: Blanco-Casini 2013
sources.role: For infinitesimally different states, the first-law relation uses the expectation of the modular Hamiltonian of the reference state: first-order variation does not by itself imply a derivative of the modular generator.

sources.label: Faulkner-Leigh-Parrikar-Wang 2016
sources.role: First-order changes of modular Hamiltonians arise when the region/family is deformed; the derivative belongs to the deformed family, not to the fixed modular flow itself.
